name: Dorothy E. Smith
shortBio: Canadian sociologist who founded feminist standpoint theory in sociology and institutional ethnography, exposing how 'relations of ruling' organize everyday lived experience through textual mediation.
centralQuestion: How do seemingly neutral sociological concepts and institutional texts conceal the standpoint of ruling power from the actualities of everyday lived work?

keyWorks.title: The Everyday World as Problematic: A Feminist Sociology
keyWorks.description: Establishes institutional ethnography and feminist standpoint sociology starting from embodied everyday experience rather than abstract bureaucratic categories.

keyWorks.title: The Conceptual Practices of Power
keyWorks.description: Investigates how sociological texts construct objectified 'ruling relations' that erase situated knowers.
